Operator: Good day, and welcome to the SecureNet Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you would like to ask a question. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss SecureNet Technologies' results for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer, and Morgan Patel, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. SecureNet Technologies had an exceptional third quarter, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. We are seeing significant traction with our cloud-native security platform and are benefiting from the increased focus on cybersecurity across all industries. The impact of our new AI-powered threat detection is evident in the reduced incident response times reported by our customers, with many seeing mean-time-to-respond improvements of over 60% in high-stakes environments.

Our strategy is centered around five core pillars: raising the bar on our full-year revenue and profitability outlook through accelerated bookings and operating leverage; amplifying channel partner performance as they drive the majority of our revenue growth; sustaining strong ARR growth rates both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year; minimizing churn through proactive customer success and platform stickiness; and delivering outsized performance from key product lines like our cloud security and SASE offerings.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we had a remarkable third quarter. Revenue reached $262 million, reflecting a 32% year-over-year increase. This growth was fueled by both new customer acquisition and expansion within our existing customer base. Our gross margin remained strong at 82%, demonstrating our ability to scale efficiently. Operating expenses were $150 million, and net income was $45 million, translating to $0.85 per share. We are increasing our guidance for the full year based on these outstanding results.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before I dive deeper into the numbers, as always, please note that our forward-looking guidance is subject to the risks and uncertainties outlined in our SEC filings, including evolving geopolitical tensions, macroeconomic headwinds like persistent inflation, and the dynamic nature of cyber threats such as the recent surge in AI-orchestrated phishing campaigns we've seen post-ChatGPT proliferation.

Let me start with the headline on our full-year revenue and profitability outlook: For full fiscal year 2024, we are raising our revenue guidance to a range of $3.25 billion to $3.35 billion, representing approximately 22% to 26% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. This compares favorably to our prior guide of $3.1 billion to $3.2 billion and reflects stronger-than-expected Q3 bookings acceleration, driven by multi-year deal ramps in our Cloud Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) and Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) portfolios. Subscription revenue, which now comprises 92% of total ARR—up from 88% last year—continues to be the growth engine, with dollar-based net retention now stabilizing at 118%, bolstered by upsell opportunities in our Falcon platform, akin to the module-adoption trends we've observed at peers like CrowdStrike.

Breaking it down by segment for clarity: Endpoint and Workload Protection is expected to deliver $1.45 billion, or about 45% of total revenue, growing 28% year-over-year. This is fueled by the global EDR/XDR convergence, where our next-gen endpoint detection and response solution has captured share from legacy players like Symantec Endpoint Protection. Key wins include a $150 million TCV deal with a Fortune 50 financial services firm, implementing our AI-driven behavioral analytics to counter ransomware families like LockBit 3.0.

Cloud Security, now our fastest-growing segment at $1.05 billion, up 35% year-over-year, representing 32% of the mix. The CNAPP market is exploding—Gartner pegs it at $10 billion TAM by 2025—and our Prisma Cloud competitor, integrated with zero-trust network access, has seen 45% quarter-over-quarter ACV expansion. We're benefiting from hyperscaler migrations to AWS Outposts and Azure Arc, with notable deployments shielding against supply chain risks reminiscent of the SolarWinds breach.

Network and Identity Security: $550 million, flat-to-up 10% year-over-year, as we lap tough comps from last year's SASE land-and-expand cycles. Here, our partnership with Zscaler on SD-WAN orchestration is yielding 20% attach rates to core subscriptions.

Professional Services and Other: $200 million, roughly 6% of revenue, with margins expanding to 25% gross due to higher utilization of our global SOC-as-a-Service, now powered by our proprietary GenAI threat hunting engine, which reduced mean-time-to-detect by 40% in beta trials.

Regionally, the Americas remain our powerhouse at 65% of revenue ($2.1 billion to $2.2 billion, +24% year-over-year), propelled by U.S. federal mandates under CMMC 2.0 and FISMA updates, where we've secured 15% market share in DoD-compliant endpoint solutions. EMEA grows to $750 million (+22% year-over-year), despite Brexit-related FX volatility, thanks to NIS2 Directive compliance driving adoption in banking—think Deutsche Bank-scale logos. APAC/Japan rounds out at $400 million (+18% year-over-year), tempered by China's data sovereignty regs but accelerated by Japanese SOC expansions amid rising APT41 nation-state activity.

On profitability, we're guiding to non-GAAP operating margins of 28% to 30%, up from 26% last year and ahead of our prior 27% outlook. This 400 basis point expansion stems from operating leverage: sales & marketing efficiency improving to 42% of revenue (down from 45%) via our revamped partner ecosystem—now 55% of bookings through MSSPs like Accenture and Deloitte—while R&D holds steady at 18% to fuel innovations like our Quantum-Resistant Cryptography suite, preempting harvest-now-decrypt-later threats from adversaries like China's PLA Unit 61398.

Non-GAAP EPS is now projected at $4.85 to $4.95, implying 25% growth on ~5% share count reduction from our ongoing $500 million buyback authorization. Free cash flow margins hit 32%, supporting $800 million in share repurchases and a potential tuck-in M&A, like our recent acquisition of a GenAI deception tech startup to enhance our autonomous SOC capabilities.

Strategically, this outlook underscores three pillars: AI/ML infusion across the stack—our Falcon Fusion SOAR now processes 10 petabytes/day of telemetry, outpacing Palo Alto's Cortex XSOAR in hunt speed; platform consolidation in a post-consolidation market, where IDC forecasts 20% CAGR through 2027 amid SASE megatrends; and resilience to macro pressures, with 95% of contracts non-cancelable and average duration at 38 months.

We're positioned to outperform the ~15% industry growth consensus from Gartner, capturing share in a $200 billion+ addressable market fragmented by point solutions.

Diving deeper into channel partner performance and contribution to revenue, which continues to be a cornerstone of our go-to-market strategy in the cybersecurity landscape. Our partner ecosystem—comprising distributors, value-added resellers, managed service providers, managed security service providers, and strategic alliances with hyperscalers—drove 68% of our total revenue this quarter, up from 62% a year ago. That's $178 million out of our record $262 million quarterly top line, reflecting a robust 32% year-over-year growth in channel bookings, outpacing our direct sales growth of 18%.

On composition: Distributors like TD Synnex and Ingram Micro accounted for 42% of channel revenue, up 25% year-over-year, fueled by their scale in mid-market deals for our SecureNet XDR platform. VARs and system integrators contributed 35%, with standout performance in large enterprise transactions—average deal size here hit $1.2 million in annual contract value, a 22% increase, driven by bundled deployments of our next-gen endpoint detection and response and cloud workload protection modules. MSSPs and MSPs rounded out 23%, growing 45% year-over-year as partners increasingly white-label our managed detection and response services to address the surging demand post high-profile incidents like the Change Healthcare ransomware attack earlier this year.

Regionally, the Americas remain our powerhouse at 52% of channel mix, delivering $92.6 million with 28% year-over-year growth. Key wins included a $15 million multi-year deal with a top-five VAR in the U.S. financial sector for zero-trust network access integrated with our SASE fabric—perfectly timed amid regulatory pressures from the SEC's cybersecurity disclosure rules. EMEA grew even faster at 38% year-over-year to $53.4 million, or 30% of channel revenue, bolstered by NIS2 Directive compliance driving adoption of our SIEM and UEBA stack. Partners like Computacenter and Bechtle were instrumental here, with co-sell motions yielding 15% higher win rates. APAC, at 18% of the mix or $32 million, accelerated 29% year-over-year despite macroeconomic headwinds; our investments in Japan and India paid off, with MSSP partners like NTT pushing our AI-powered threat hunting capabilities into telco and critical infrastructure verticals amid rising state-sponsored threats.

Technically, we've supercharged partner enablement through our SecureNet Partner Accelerator Program, launched in Q4 last year. We've certified over 7,200 partner engineers on our unified XDR platform—up 60% quarter-over-quarter—including hands-on labs for integrating with Palo Alto's Prisma Cloud and AWS Security Hub. This has translated to a 25% uplift in partner-sourced pipeline, now at $1.8 billion for the back half of FY2024, with 40% from top-10 partners who represent 45% of channel revenue. Renewal dynamics are stellar too: Channel net revenue retention clocked in at 118%, versus 112% direct, thanks to expanded footprints in multi-product deals—our 'Land and Expand' playbook is yielding 35% upsell attach rates on initial EDR wins.

Strategically, this performance underscores our conviction in a channel-first model amid industry tailwinds: global cybersecurity spending projected to hit $212 billion in 2024 per Gartner, with 75% flowing through partners. We're doubling down with $50 million in FY2024 partner incentives, including SPIFs for MDR and GenAI security upsells—critical as vulnerabilities like those in Ivanti and Citrix expose gaps in legacy tools. We've also deepened hyperscaler integrations, co-engineering with Microsoft Azure for native Sentinel interoperability, which unlocked 12 new MSSP logos this quarter. Looking forward, we expect channel contribution to reach 72% by FYE, with ACV per partner deal climbing another 15% on subscription momentum. Risks remain—supply chain disruptions from geopolitical tensions could pressure distributor inventories—but our 95% partner satisfaction score in our latest NPS survey positions us to capture share from point solutions like legacy antivirus players.

This channel strength not only diversifies our revenue but fortifies our competitive moat in an XDR-consolidated market.

Turning to ARR growth rate, both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year, which remains the cornerstone of our subscription-based SaaS model in the cybersecurity landscape. ARR ended the quarter at $452 million, reflecting robust sequential and year-over-year momentum amid a market grappling with escalating threats like ransomware-as-a-service campaigns and nation-state APTs.

On a quarter-over-quarter basis, ARR grew 14% from $396 million in Q2, outpacing our guidance midpoint and signaling strong execution in our land-and-expand strategy. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit quarter-over-quarter growth, driven by a healthy mix of new customer additions and expansions within our existing base.

Year-over-year, we're up an impressive 38%, expanding from $328 million in Q3 2023. This significantly outperforms the broader cybersecurity market's estimated 18-20% year-over-year ARR growth, as reported by Gartner and IDC, and positions us ahead of peers like CrowdStrike, which posted 33% year-over-year in their last quarter, and Palo Alto Networks at around 25% for their Prisma Cloud segment. Our dollar-based net retention rate held steady at 128% for the full year, reflecting sticky adoption of our platform as customers consolidate point solutions amid economic headwinds.

Breaking down the drivers, new logo ARR contributed $28 million, or about 6% quarter-over-quarter growth, fueled by our NexusAI endpoint detection and response solution, which saw 45% quarter-over-quarter adoption growth among mid-market enterprises. We've seen particular traction in sectors like financial services and healthcare, where regulatory pressures—think SEC cyber disclosure rules and HIPAA expansions—are accelerating zero-trust architectures. Expansions and upsells added another $22 million, with our average net expansion rate hitting 115% for customers with over $100K in ARR. A prime example is our integration with Microsoft Sentinel SIEM, which drove multi-million-dollar upsells for 15% of our top 100 accounts, as clients migrate from legacy tools like Splunk.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, accounting for 62% of total ARR with 16% quarter-over-quarter and 42% year-over-year growth. Demand here is propelled by supply chain vulnerabilities echoing Log4j and SolarWinds, pushing Fortune 500 CISOs toward our cloud-native secure access service edge stack. EMEA surged 22% quarter-over-quarter, representing 24% of ARR, thanks to NIS2 Directive compliance and a wave of GDPR fines—we've landed key wins with European banks adopting our SecureNet XDR for unified threat visibility. APAC, now 12% of ARR, grew 18% quarter-over-quarter on the back of Southeast Asian digital transformation and rising state-sponsored attacks from groups like Lazarus; partnerships with AWS Tokyo and Azure Singapore have been pivotal. LatAm is our fastest-growing region at 28% year-over-year, albeit from a smaller base, as Brazilian PIX payment rails expose new attack surfaces.

Strategically, these trends underscore our pivot to AI-infused, platform-led cybersecurity. In Q3, we rolled out NexusAI 2.0, leveraging generative AI for autonomous threat hunting—early pilots with beta customers like a major U.S. retailer reduced mean time to respond by 65%. We've also deepened hyperscaler integrations, including a co-sell agreement with Google Cloud that contributed $15 million in pipeline acceleration. Looking ahead, we expect Q4 2024 ARR growth of 13-15% quarter-over-quarter and 36-40% year-over-year, supported by a $2.1 billion RPO—up 45% year-over-year—with current remaining performance obligations growing even faster at 52%. Risks like macro slowdowns could pressure win rates, but our 95% gross retention and focus on high-velocity deals with SMBs via our channel partners—think Ingram Micro and TD Synnex—mitigate that.

In summary, our ARR trajectory validates SecureNet's leadership in the $80 billion-plus cybersecurity market, where consolidation and AI are reshaping the playbook. We're not just growing; we're compounding value for customers fortifying against an evolving threatscape.

On churn rate and reasons for churn, a critical leading indicator for our long-term ARR growth in the cybersecurity SaaS landscape. For context, we track three key churn metrics: gross logo churn, which measures customer seat losses; gross dollar churn, capturing revenue attrition; and our flagship net revenue retention rate, which factors in expansions, upsells, and cross-sells against downsells and churn.

In Q3, our gross dollar churn came in at 4.2% quarterly, annualizing to approximately 8.1%—a 120 basis point improvement from Q2's 5.4% and down 310 bps year-over-year. This marks our lowest quarterly churn in three years, reflecting the stickiness of our integrated Zero Trust platform, which now powers endpoint detection and response, secure access service edge, and cloud workload protection for over 85% of our top 500 customers. Logo churn was even stronger at 3.1%, driven by our enterprise focus where multi-year contracts now represent 72% of total ARR, up from 65% a year ago.

Our NRR held steady at 118% for the quarter—well above the cybersecurity peer average of 110% as reported in recent Bessemer Venture Partners' State of the Cloud Index. This expansion dynamic more than offsets any gross churn, with $42 million in net expansion revenue in Q3 alone, fueled by 142 upsell deals averaging 28% ACV increase per customer. To put this in perspective, our large enterprise cohort (customers >$1M ARR) delivered a segment NRR of 125%, compared to 112% in the SMB segment, highlighting the value of our platform consolidation play amid the post-SolarWinds and Log4j era of supply chain scrutiny.

Breaking down the primary reasons for churn, based on our post-cancellation win/loss analysis covering 97% of departed logos. We've categorized them into four buckets, with clear trends and mitigations:

Macroeconomic and budget pressures accounted for 32% of churn, down from 41% year-over-year. The ongoing high interest rate environment and IT budget scrutiny—echoed in Gartner’s 2024 CIO surveys showing 28% of cybersecurity spend deferred—drove some mid-market renewals to non-renew. Notably, 18% of these were in verticals like retail and manufacturing facing margin compression from inflation. We've countered this aggressively with our 'SecureNet Flex' pricing model, introduced in Q4 last year, which allows 20-30% usage-based scaling without full commitment risk. This initiative recovered 15 deals at risk, contributing to a 22% reduction in budget-related churn quarter-over-quarter.

Mergers, acquisitions, and rationalization made up 25% of churn. M&A activity remains elevated, with 47% of our churn tied to consolidations where duplicate tools get sunsetted—similar to what we've seen industry-wide post-Microsoft's Activision deal ripple effects. Key example: Two Fortune 1000 customers in financial services churned after acquiring targets with entrenched CrowdStrike Falcon deployments. Our strategic response? Deepening our partner ecosystem integrations, including API parity with Palo Alto Networks' Prisma Cloud and Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange, which has increased our win rate in M&A scenarios to 68% per our Q3 sales ops data.

Competitive displacement was 22% of churn, flat year-over-year. Pure competition accounted for about one in five losses, primarily to point solutions like SentinelOne's Singularity for EDR-heavy workloads or Okta's identity stack in IAM-focused accounts. A standout case was a healthcare provider switching to Wiz for cloud-native app sec, citing faster vulnerability prioritization. However, we've clawed back momentum with our Q2 launch of 'NetAI Sentinel,' our GenAI-powered threat hunting module, which boasts 40% faster mean-time-to-detect on ransomware variants per MITRE ATT&CK evaluations. This has flipped 11 competitive threats into expansions year-to-date.

Product fit and support gaps were 21% of churn, down sharply 15% year-over-year. Early gaps in our SASE offerings for high-latency APAC networks led to some dissatisfaction, but our R&D investments—$180 million in FY24, or 22% of revenue—have addressed this. For instance, edge-native SD-WAN optimizations reduced latency by 35% in beta tests, retaining 92% of at-risk APAC logos.

Regionally, performance varies as expected in our global footprint: North America (62% of ARR) had best-in-class gross dollar churn of 3.4%, bolstered by sticky FedRAMP High authorization for our CWP module, securing 14 new U.S. government contracts worth $28 million ARR. EMEA (24% of ARR): 4.8% churn, pressured by GDPR compliance shifts but offset by DACH region strength where our data sovereignty features won against local players like Sophos. APAC (9% of ARR, 5% of bookings): Highest at 6.7%, due to sovereign cloud mandates in China and India, plus yen depreciation impacting Japanese budgets. That said, our Singapore hub expansions and partnerships with NTT and Telstra have driven 145% year-over-year bookings growth here, with churn trending down 200 bps sequentially.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on sub-7% annualized dollar churn by FY25 through three pillars: Proactive Customer Success, with our 1:50 CS-to-ACV ratio team deploying AI-driven health scoring, flagging 320 at-risk accounts early and achieving 87% retention uplift; Platform Lock-in, where 68% of customers now use 4+ modules, per our 'Land-and-Expand' playbook, mirroring successes at peers like ServiceNow; Economic Moats, leveraging macroeconomic tailwinds like the 300% year-over-year surge in ransomware claims per Chainalysis, we're bundling cyber insurance integrations via partners like Coalition, which has extended average contract duration to 28 months.

In summary, our churn profile underscores SecureNet's resilience in a maturing cybersecurity market projected to hit $250 billion by 2028 per IDC. With NRR north of 115% and expansions accelerating, we're well-positioned for 25%+ ARR growth in FY24.

Finally, on the performance of key product lines like cloud security and SASE, where we continue to see robust demand driven by the accelerating shift to hybrid workforces, multi-cloud environments, and the relentless evolution of sophisticated threats like ransomware-as-a-service and nation-state APTs. Our cloud security and SASE portfolios were standout performers this quarter, representing 68% of total revenue—up from 62% a year ago—and delivering combined year-over-year growth of 42%.

Cloud Security posted $178 million in Q3 revenue, a blistering 51% year-over-year increase and 28% quarter-over-quarter growth. This marks our 11th straight quarter of 50%+ year-over-year growth in this line, fueled by enterprises grappling with sprawling multi-cloud footprints. Annual Recurring Revenue for Cloud Security now stands at $812 million, with dollar-based net retention expanding to 128%—reflecting strong upsell momentum as customers consolidate point solutions onto our unified platform.

Key drivers include our Zero Trust Cloud Architecture initiative, launched last quarter, which integrates runtime behavioral analytics powered by our GenAI threat detection models. We've seen a 35% reduction in mean-time-to-remediate for cloud misconfigurations in beta customers, with early adopters like a Fortune 50 financial services firm reporting 40% fewer vulnerabilities post-deployment. Tactically, we've deepened integrations with AWS Bedrock, Azure Sentinel, and Google Cloud's Chronicle, enabling seamless data lake federation for anomaly detection across hyperscalers.

Regionally, the Americas drove 62% of Cloud Security bookings, with hyperscaler-aligned wins in financial services and healthcare—sectors hit hard by Log4Shell remnants and supply chain exploits. EMEA accelerated to 25% year-over-year growth, boosted by NIS2 Directive compliance tailwinds; we landed six-figure ACV deals with two DAX 40 manufacturers adopting our CWPP for Kubernetes-orchestrated environments. APAC, while still nascent at 13% of bookings, surged 72% year-over-year on PDI mandates in Japan and surging AWS Outposts adoption in India.

Strategically, we're outpacing the Gartner-projected 25% CAGR for CNAPPs through our M&A playbook—our acquisition of SkyWard Analytics last year has supercharged our DSPM capabilities, contributing 15% to Q3 growth. Looking ahead, we'll preview at Black Hat our "CloudShield AI Guardian," a fully autonomous agent for predictive drift detection, targeting 20% ARR uplift in Q4.

Shifting to SASE, our Secure Access Service Edge platform—blending ZTNA, FWaaS, SWG, and CASB with native SD-WAN—delivered $142 million in Q3 revenue, up 38% year-over-year and representing 22% sequential growth. Total SASE ARR hit $621 million, with Remaining Performance Obligations growing 55% year-over-year to $1.2 billion, underscoring multi-year commit strength. We added 247 net new logos, including 14 seven-figure deals, pushing our large-customer cohort (10,000+ employees) to 68% of SASE ACV.

Performance here is propelled by the "secure edge" megatrend: with 65% of enterprises now running 50%+ workloads at the edge per our Q3 Customer Pulse Survey, SASE is no longer optional. Our platform's 99.999% uptime SLA and sub-50ms latency via Anycast PoPs (now 180 globally) have differentiated us against incumbents like Zscaler and Cisco Secure Connect. A technical highlight is our SASE Fusion Engine, which leverages eBPF for microsegmentation and ML-driven DLP at line rate—resulting in a 62% year-over-year increase in traffic inspected, now exceeding 15 exabytes quarterly.

Regionally, APAC led with 48% year-over-year growth, capturing share in high-growth markets like Singapore and Australia amid 5G rollout and sovereign cloud pushes; we displaced legacy VPNs at three telcos there. The Americas remained steady at 52% of bookings, with expansions in retail and energy verticals defending against Magecart-style attacks. EMEA grew 32% year-over-year, aided by Schrems II compliance and our partnership with Deutsche Telekom for carrier-grade SASE delivery.

On strategy, our 118% NRR reflects sticky expansions—average deal size swelled 24% year-over-year as customers layer on our iPaaS module. We've filed three new patents around quantum-resistant encryption for SASE tunnels, positioning us for post-quantum readiness. Forward guidance: Expect SASE to comprise 30% of total revenue by FYE '25, accelerated by our planned integration of Cato Networks-inspired mesh routing in Q4.

Across both lines, AI-infused innovations—like our ThreatXchange federated learning consortium with CrowdStrike and SentinelOne—have driven 25% of Q3 upsells, while ransomware mitigation features (e.g., immutable backups in Cloud Security) addressed the 37% year-over-year surge in attacks per Chainalysis data. Margins expanded 420 basis points to 82% gross in these segments, thanks to 40% cloud-native efficiencies.

In summary, Cloud Security and SASE are not just growing—they're redefining cybersecurity perimeters in a zero-trust world. We're gaining share in a $75 billion addressable market per IDC estimates, with Q4 guidance calling for 40-45% combined growth.

Next, Taylor Kim will provide more technical details.

Taylor Kim: Thank you, Jordan. We continue to innovate and push the boundaries of what's possible in cybersecurity. Our team is focused on developing cutting-edge solutions that address the evolving threat landscape. We are investing heavily in research and development to stay ahead of the curve and deliver unparalleled value to our customers. Key areas of focus include advancing our AI/ML capabilities across the platform, such as the NexusAI 2.0 for autonomous threat hunting that reduced MTTR by 65% in pilots, deepening hyperscaler integrations like those with AWS Bedrock and Azure Sentinel for seamless anomaly detection, and rolling out innovations like CloudShield AI Guardian for predictive drift detection in CNAPP environments. Our Quantum-Resistant Cryptography suite and SASE Fusion Engine with eBPF microsegmentation ensure we're preempting future threats like harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks while handling 15 exabytes of quarterly traffic at line rate.

Morgan Patel: Thank you. Cybersecurity is paramount, and we are taking proactive measures to protect our customers and ourselves. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance, including FedRAMP High authorizations, NIS2 and CMMC 2.0 adherence, and robust data sovereignty features that have helped us secure DoD-compliant wins and retain 92% of at-risk APAC logos through edge optimizations.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the Q&A session. At this time, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your touchtone phone. First question comes from Ben Carter with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Carter: Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Jordan, you raised full-year guidance meaningfully—can you talk more about how you're thinking about profitability into 2025, especially with R&D steady at 18%?

Jordan Lee: Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, our 28% to 30% non-GAAP operating margins for FY24 set a strong foundation, driven by sales and marketing efficiency down to 42% of revenue through channel leverage at 55% of bookings. Heading into 2025, we see continued expansion from operating leverage, targeting 32%+ margins as free cash flow hits 32% this year, funding buybacks and tuck-ins like our GenAI deception acquisition. Platform consolidation and 95% non-cancelable contracts with 38-month durations provide resilience, even amid macro pressures.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Great, thanks. On channel partners, that 68% contribution is impressive—any color on how top partners like NTT and Accenture are performing, and risks from supply chain issues?

Jordan Lee: Hi Lisa, yes, top-10 partners drove 40% of channel revenue, with NTT excelling in APAC telco amid APT41 threats, and Accenture in Americas MSSP deals. Our Partner Accelerator certified 7,200 engineers, up 60% QoQ, lifting pipeline 25%. Geopolitical supply chain risks are noted, but 95% partner NPS mitigates, positioning us for 72% channel mix by FYE.

Operator: Next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez: Thanks. Taylor, on the product side, how is the GenAI threat hunting integrating with SASE and cloud security, and any early metrics?

Taylor Kim: Thanks, Mike. Our GenAI engine is fully infused—Falcon Fusion SOAR processes 10 petabytes daily, faster than peers, while SASE Fusion with ML-DLP inspects 15 exabytes quarterly. In cloud, GuardAI Sentinel cut MTTD 40% on ransomware per MITRE, and pilots show 65% MTTR reduction. ThreatXchange consortium with CrowdStrike drives 25% upsells.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Patel with Barclays.

Emily Patel: Solid results. Alex, with churn at 4.2% gross dollar, how are you addressing competitive displacements, especially in APAC?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Emily. Competitive churn at 22% is stable, but we've flipped threats with NetAI Sentinel outperforming SentinelOne in EDR and Wiz in cloud prioritization. In APAC, SD-WAN latency fixes retained 92%, and NTT/Telstra partnerships grew bookings 145% YoY despite sovereign regs. Proactive CS with AI health scoring uplifts retention 87%, targeting sub-7% annualized by FY25.

Alex Rivera: Thank you all for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. Thank you to our dedicated employees, loyal customers, and valued partners.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
